Test for Temporal or Model-Version Scoring Drift

Source: R/drift.R
check_drift.Rd

Evaluates whether LLM scores on a shared anchor set of texts drift across timepoints, waves, or model versions. Performs an overall within-unit drift test across versions plus pairwise comparisons against a baseline version (paired mean shift, paired Cohen's \(d_z\), variance ratio, rank/agreement stability, and Kolmogorov-Smirnov distributional shift).

Usage

check_drift(
  data,
  score_col = "score",
  version_col = "version",
  id_col = "unit_id",
  baseline = NULL,
  truth_col = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  min_effect = 0.2,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

An llm_coded_data object or a data.frame.

score_col

Name of the numeric LLM score column.

version_col

Name of the column identifying timepoint, wave, or model version (must have at least 2 distinct values).

id_col

Name of the anchor unit identifier column. Default "unit_id".

baseline

Optional value in version_col serving as the reference version. Defaults to the first factor level (or first sorted unique value).

truth_col

Optional name of a human gold-standard score column to track calibration bias and RMSE drift across versions.

alpha

Significance level for drift flagging. Default 0.05.

min_effect

Minimum absolute paired Cohen's \(d_z\) required alongside statistical significance to trigger drift_flag. Default 0.20.

na.rm

Logical; drop missing rows. Default TRUE.

Value

An S3 object of class "llm_drift" containing:

  • summary: tibble of per-version statistics and pairwise drift tests vs baseline.

  • overall_test: tibble summarizing the omnibus within-unit test across all versions.

  • baseline: reference version label.

  • drift_detected: logical scalar (TRUE if any version triggers drift).

  • alpha, min_effect, version_col, score_col, data.

Examples

set.seed(1)
anchor <- tibble::tibble(
  unit_id = rep(paste0("u", 1:40), 3),
  version = rep(c("v1", "v2", "v3"), each = 40),
  base = rep(rnorm(40), 3),
  score = base + rep(c(0, 0.05, 0.55), each = 40) + rnorm(120, 0, 0.25)
)
check_drift(anchor, score_col = "score", version_col = "version")
#> 
#> ── LLM Scoring Drift Diagnostics 
#> Baseline: "v1" | Overall ANOVA F(2, 78) = 43.315, p = <0.0001
#> Drift detected (alpha=0.05, |d_z|>=0.2): TRUE
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   version n_shared mean_diff cohens_dz   icc p_adj drift_flag
#>   <chr>      <int>     <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>     
#> 1 v1            40     0         0     1     1     FALSE     
#> 2 v2            40     0.049     0.174 0.952 0.277 FALSE     
#> 3 v3            40     0.442     1.15  0.832 0     TRUE
